sections.html:
Three county offices cover it, and the first two sit in the Government Center at 150 North Queen Street in Lancaster. Property Assessment sets values, the Treasurer takes county tax payments, and the Tax Claim Bureau, listed under the Treasurer, collects taxes that have gone delinquent.

  • Property Assessment: Suite 310, building entrance on Chestnut Street, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., phone 717-299-8381.
  • Treasurer: Suite 122, phone 717-299-8222, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, with a 9:00 a.m. start on the second Thursday of each month and early or late appointments available.
  • Tax Claim Bureau: delinquent tax reports, sale notices and the repository list are posted on its county page.

The county, 17 school districts and most of the 60 municipalities levy a property tax, so a Lancaster County tax bill is really several bills. The Assessment Office tracks more than 195,000 parcels for them.

The county uses fair market value, meaning the price a willing seller and a willing buyer would agree on in an arm's length sale. A three-member Board of Assessment Appeals hears disputes about it.

The last full reassessment took effect on January 1, 2018, with values pegged to market value as of that date at a 100 percent ratio. A new countywide reassessment sets values for tax year 2027. The county says a reassessment aims to equalize values rather than raise taxes, because the county, the municipalities and the school districts must adjust their millage so their income does not rise. A taxing body can still raise its rate afterward, as in any other year.

Property records are free to view on the county site, and the county warns owners not to pay for a copy of their record.

A standard appeal is due August 1 each year. When the Assessment Office changes a value, you have 40 days from the change notice. Countywide reassessments follow a separate rule.

Lancaster County assessment appeal types
Appeal typeDeadlineFiling fee
Annual appealAugust 1Varies by property class, per parcel
Change of assessment (40-day appeal)40 days from the change noticeNone
Reassessment appeal40 days from the notice or August 1, whichever is laterNone in the year notices are mailed

File one application per parcel with the Board at the Assessment Office, in person or by mail. The owner of record signs it, or an officer for a company, or a representative under a power of attorney.

sections.h2: If you missed the 2027 reassessment appeal
sections.html:
The 2027 reassessment appeal deadline has closed. The county's Property Assessment page says the next annual appeal opportunity is 2028, with more information due in early 2027.

A 40-day appeal can still follow a change of assessment notice, which the office issues after a property's market value changes.

  • An appeal challenges the assessed value of the property. It says nothing about the amount of tax owed.
  • Tax rates differ by municipality and school district, so equal assessments can produce different bills.
  • The county asks owners to consider whether they could sell for the new assessed figure before they file.

sections.h2: What happens at an appeal hearing
sections.html:
The Board mails the date, time and place to the owner of record, who must tell any representative or witness. Each case takes roughly 5 to 15 minutes, and anyone who testifies signs an oath. The purpose is to determine market value, so evidence counts for more than argument.

  • A certified appraisal.
  • A recent deed showing the price paid in an arm's length sale.
  • Recent sales of similar properties.
  • A market value analysis prepared by a Realtor.
  • For commercial and industrial property, leases, rent schedules and income and expense reports.

A decision arrives later by mail. The Board can dismiss an appeal when the owner fails to appear or to produce requested documents, so bring paper, not just an opinion.

The Assessment Office keeps homestead enrollment information. Recent applications may not show on its website yet, and anyone who has just bought a property should contact the office. Phone before you assume the exclusion is on your record.

Rural parcels sometimes sit in a preferential land program. If yours might, ask the Assessment Office whether the parcel is enrolled and what a sale or a split of the land would change, and get that answer in writing before you sign a contract.

The Tax Claim Bureau steps in on unpaid taxes. It posts a delinquent tax report on its county page, and the total due can change because interest accrues monthly on the first day of a new month. If you owe back taxes, ask for a current payoff figure close to the closing date.

The bureau also runs upset and judicial tax sales, announced in notices on the county site, and keeps a repository list of properties that did not sell. If your property is facing one, call the bureau before the sale date instead of waiting for the notice.

The Real Estate Tax page offers a Request for Waiver of Additional Charges form, which is the route to ask for relief from added penalties. The county decides whether to grant it.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller, in order
sections.html:
Pull your property record from the county site first, since it is free. Next, compare the assessed value with what you expect to list at. If the two are far apart, think about whether a change of assessment notice or a future appeal makes sense, keeping the deadlines above in mind.

Then call the Treasurer at 717-299-8222 about the county bill and the Tax Claim Bureau if anything is delinquent. Finally, tell your title company early so it can order the certification and confirm the municipal and school bills before the closing date.

sections.h2: What to do about property tax before you sell
sections.html:
Start with the numbers the county already holds. The Treasurer's page offers a way to pay a county tax bill online, a tax search for Lancaster County properties and a tax certification service. Ask the title company to order the certification and to verify that municipal and school bills are also paid.

  • Check the 2027 reassessment value against your list price, since buyers will look it up.
  • Confirm which tax collector handles your municipality and school district for the current bill.
  • Settle proration of the year's taxes in the sales contract.

The median value of owner-occupied homes in Lancaster County is $301,100 for 2020 to 2024, and 69.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied. For a house that needs work or has tax trouble, the closing steps are the same, but a cash sale can shorten them.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a Lancaster County assessment?
faqs.a: August 1 each year for an annual appeal, or 40 days from a change of assessment notice. The 2027 reassessment deadline has closed, and the county says the next annual appeal opportunity is 2028.

faqs.q: Does it cost money to appeal an assessment in Lancaster County?
faqs.a: It depends on the type. Annual appeals carry a fee that varies by property class, charged per parcel. Change of assessment appeals have no fee, and reassessment appeals are free in the year notices are mailed.

faqs.q: Will my Lancaster County taxes go up after the 2027 reassessment?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The county, municipalities and school districts must adjust their millage so reassessment does not increase their income. Final rates are set later, and any rate change is a separate decision by each taxing body.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Lancaster County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's office at 150 North Queen Street, Suite 122, takes payments, and the county site has an option to pay the county tax bill online. Call 717-299-8222 for hours that suit your schedule.

faqs.q: Who handles delinquent taxes in Lancaster County?
faqs.a: The Tax Claim Bureau, which is part of the Treasurer's office. Its delinquent tax report changes because interest is added on the first day of each month. It also holds the upset and judicial tax sales.
